findings.title: Rescheduling still creates SendGrid pending cancellations immediately
findings.body: Passing `true` takes the immediate-cancellation branch, which POSTs a cancel status to SendGrid instead of marking the reminder `cancelled` for the cron job. SendGrid retains these pending cancellations until the scheduled date, so repeated reschedules can still hit the 100-cancellation limit and cause later reminders to be sent—the failure this PR is intended to prevent.

findings.title: A reminder can be sent before the next cancellation cron run
findings.body: This selects cancelled reminders only when this endpoint runs; with a 15-minute cron interval, a booking cancelled just after a run can have a reminder scheduled less than 15 minutes away. The next run may occur after SendGrid has sent it, so cancellation is not guaranteed for reminders close to their scheduled time.

findings.title: Cancellation updates are not awaited before the handler returns
findings.body: These async cancellation calls are started without awaiting them, and the handler does not wait for them later. In particular, the email helper must persist `cancelled: true` for the cron job to cancel the SendGrid send; the booking cancellation response can complete before that write finishes, and a serverless runtime may terminate the invocation before it does, leaving the reminder eligible to be sent.
